change: Compare String-owned buffers directly instead of cloning both; return true for an identical receiver/argument only after validating the receiver representation.

contract.before: Validate and clone the left String, attempt to clone the right String, then compare byte vectors. Invalid receivers fail; non-String arguments answer false.
contract.after: Validate the left String in its owner table, handle self-equality, otherwise validate the right table entry and compare the same bytes under one private immutable borrow.
review: No dependency message or callback occurs while the buffer table is borrowed.
No foreign payload access, normalization change, cached method or new object representation.
The identity shortcut cannot bypass receiver validation; the captured-method test checks a non-String receiver compared with itself.
Current Id method lookup still selects the equality implementation; public behavior and result identities are unchanged.

microbenchmark.scope: Existing String equality through Id on 16-byte, 4-KiB and 1-MiB inputs: equal distinct objects, same object, first-byte mismatch and last-byte mismatch. Five samples/process; serial ABBA. Normal GC policy; no managed allocations in the equality body. Every result checked.

validation: Expanded String/Error test checks equal distinct binary Strings, self-equality, unequal contents, non-String arguments, and invalid self-receiver rejection.
Full Oop core/compiler/GC and negative dispatch/construction contracts.
limits: Local CPU microbenchmarks, not whole-application speedups.
Normal GC policy; equality itself creates no managed objects. Removed copies were native temporary allocations.
Only String differs in the comparison prefixes. The installed user runtime was not replaced.
